Both the Efficiency and Fill factor simulated from I–V curves are more or less matched with practical data and the samples remain stable as there is less fluctuations of the simulated parameters from the practically obtained values.

articleTitle: A sustainable energy model focusing renewable energy: A case study for poultry farms in Bangladesh
publicationTitle: 2014 3rd International Conference on the Developments in Renewable Energy Technology (ICDRET)
abstract: According to “Bangladesh Economic Rivew-2013”, the number of registered poultry farms in Bangladesh till February, 2013 is about 65902. This is believed to be more than two hundred thousand by non-government statistics. The number is increasing rapidly with the growing demand of protein and dependency on poultry-birds for this. Each and every farm draws certain amount of electric power. Most of these farms draw power from the national grid; some of them use natural gas or diesel generators and very few farms use their own poultry droppings for producing biogas and generating electricity. Unfortunately, these few biogas plants not even run to the peak of their capacity. The over reliance on national grid and fossil fuels aids to the emission of greenhouse gases and it is going to spiral up every year. If these poultry farms could produce sufficient energy from the poultry droppings then their annual costs, greenhouse gas emission as well as fossil fuel dependency will become nominal. The aim of this study is to reveal the prospect of self-sufficient poultry farms using their poultry droppings only. A comparison is made among the annual costs, energy efficiency and greenhouse gases emissions from different sources of energy or different mix of them. It is seen that coproduction of electricity and fertilizer optimize the mentioned constraints.

articleTitle: Possibility of a tidal power plant in Sandwip Island of Bangladesh
publicationTitle: 2014 3rd International Conference on the Developments in Renewable Energy Technology (ICDRET)
abstract: Bangladesh has long been suffering from energy starvation with its dense population of almost 160 million. Energy crisis of Bangladesh has reached to the very last level and power generation is the top priority of the present government. Government has taken some policies to increase the power generation to meet the crisis. But it is evident that in near future we have to switch from fuels to renewable sources of energy for power generation. In this paper the analysis of tidal data of 5 different sites of Bangladesh is presented to propose a suitable site to install tidal turbine for generating power from tidal source. This proposal is expected to make the best use of tidal energy available in the isolated areas and to help to solve the power crisis of the country.

articleTitle: Living in harmony: Designing a multi-functional education facility that has positive sustainable impact on environment and society
publicationTitle: 2014 3rd International Conference on the Developments in Renewable Energy Technology (ICDRET)
abstract: A unique way of teaching practical aspects of renewable energy technologies has been experimented in the University of Oldenburg since 1987. An energy laboratory (Energielabor), built in 1982 and powered by renewable energy sources, has been used for practical training, lectures and office space for the staff and students engaged in the field of renewable energy at the University. After 30 years of service, this Energielabor requires revision and needs to be rebuilt to meet the needs of present age. In this direction, as part of a module named ‘Case Study’, PPRE masters' students assessed the locally available renewable energy resources and estimated the energy demand for a newly proposed design for the upcoming new Energielabor. This paper presents the first results of these energy demand and resource assessments, along with highlighting the didactical concepts and motivations behind the newly proposed design.

articleTitle: Feasibility analysis and prospect of applications of micro concentrated solar power in Bangladesh
publicationTitle: 2014 3rd International Conference on the Developments in Renewable Energy Technology (ICDRET)
abstract: Micro concentrated solar power is a very promising technology. It uses relatively smaller solar collectors to concentrate sunlight and convert it into heat. In this paper, feasibility of micro concentrated solar power has been analyzed. Bangladesh has advantages such as solar energy, electric network, back up fossil fuels, ambient temperature for micro concentrated solar power. Among many applications of micro concentrated solar power most important applications are air conditioning, irrigation, process heat, producing electricity, desalination and solar fuels for transportation. Various applications of micro concentrated solar power hold immense potential to help Bangladesh to reduce power crisis.

articleTitle: Power calculation of GaN/AlGaN based thermo-photovoltaic heterostructure
publicationTitle: 2014 3rd International Conference on the Developments in Renewable Energy Technology (ICDRET)
abstract: Intersubband transition based multiple junction quantum cascade heterostructure has been designed for efficient photovoltaic energy conversion and to operate in higher frequency range. Our designed structure produces wider absorption spectrum, faster carrier transport as well as higher current and power density.

articleTitle: Efficiency calculation of single junction silicon solar cell at different doping concentrations
publicationTitle: 2014 3rd International Conference on the Developments in Renewable Energy Technology (ICDRET)
abstract: In this fast growing era of modern technology, the human race suffers the problem of rapid depletion of natural resources to generate as a power source. Hence to find a sublime solution of this phenomenon is a must. Solar cells are eventually proved very fruitful for this daunting task. One obstacle that hinders its potentiality is its efficiency. Low efficient solar cells will not fulfill the desired requirements. This paper handles different doping concentrations to be implemented with, in silicon based solar cell, and observes the highest possible efficiency that can be attained. For this task, TCAD device simulator has been used to create a virtual model of silicon based single junction solar cell. Therefore, we can so monitor the best outcome, how the device will behave, due to several types of concentration with the help of their efficiency and fill factor.

articleTitle: A two-seater light-weight solar powered clean car: Preliminary design and economic analysis
publicationTitle: 2014 3rd International Conference on the Developments in Renewable Energy Technology (ICDRET)
abstract: This paper outlines the design of a prototype solar powered light-weight economically affordable clean car for the daily office commuters of Dhaka city. Calculation in this paper shows that the solar power alone will be sufficient to operate a light-weight car from one end of the capital city Dhaka, to the other, for a journey to and from the office. A preliminary design of the solar car has been performed in this paper by calculating and estimating the required panel size, battery capacity and motor power. A plug-in charging option has been supplemented to the car for extracting electricity from the mains during times of insufficient energy receptions from the sun. Economic analysis performed on the life cycle cost of solar cars, as opposed to traditional fuel-based cars shows that over the long-term, solar cars come out to be much less expensive. Over a period of 20 years, combined cost of solar component replacements and electricity charges amount to a total over BDT 2 lac, which is approximately 1/9<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">th</sup> the total cost of operating a fuel-based car in Dhaka, considering the fuel cost, maintenance and annual inflation over the same duration.

articleTitle: Renewable energy programs for rural electrification: Experience and lessons from India
publicationTitle: 2014 3rd International Conference on the Developments in Renewable Energy Technology (ICDRET)
abstract: Grid electrification has been the predominant mode for electrification covering almost 94.5% of the inhabited area in India. However, renewable energy based off-grid technologies have also been disseminated extensively in the country. This paper attempts to capture the development of off-grid rural electrification through renewable energy in India and analyses the experiences and lessons, which can contribute for the better program designing and policy making.
